Q: Is it good practice to pass IRibbonUI into service classes to refresh Ribbon after async work in a VSTO Word add‑in? A:

I think this should be posted as a "normal" (newly AKA Troubleshooting/Debugging) question rather than an open-ended "best practices" one.
It should have (in principle) some clear answer(s).

Q: Pickle error: AttributeError: Can't get attribute on <module '__main__' (built-in)> A:

AttributeError: Can't get attribute '' on <module

For me it was a case of loading up a register of objects during a conversion. I want to make reruns faster so employ the pickle files. It was a case of declaring this in a global sort of scope, but defining them above the classes the Pickle file has serialised. By moving the assignment of the registry outside of function/class scope below all the classes I was including in the pickle file things worked.

eg REGISTRY = getRegistry() # This contains with open statement using rb flag.

Oddly I also got this message at one point too:

TypeError: file must have 'read' and 'readline' attributes

I think it's also a good idea to check all the properties you may define on classes are being resolved using the VS Code IDE Python debugger. 'Traceback' will be at the start of the value in the debugger for class properties that are silently failing possibly down to typos. For example missing self. off formatted string that is lazy loaded with if not hasattr. Once all that has been done things should work correctly again - and don't believe the guff Co-Pilot has to say on the issue about not being able to serialise complex objects. I've done complex object serialisation to load/dump data in another project I wrote some time ago, so I was surprised to start see issues with the copied boilerplate pickle file handling code.

Q: How to exclude a TestConfiguration from an ApplicationContextRunner in a unit test? A:

Max's answer fixed my problem, but today I realise that I was using @TestConfiguration in a unit test rather than an integration test. My unit test is annotated @SpringJUnitConfig and I add the test configuration class in that annotation. So the @TestConfiguration isn't needed here - I can just remove it and everything works.

Q: CloudKit records not deleted when removed from iOS app A:

CloudKit has three databases:

1. container.privateCloudDatabase
2. container.publicCloudDatabase
3. container.sharedCloudDatabase

if you save to privateCloudDatabase but fetch from publicCloudDatabase the delete will appear to not work. First thing to verify make sure db is the same instance for:
- save
- query
- delete
- fetch on next launch

also confirm CKContainer, CKDatabse and Zone should be same then check:
- Deletion actually returns successfully
- No automatic re-upload from local cache
- No second device restoring it
